svg.title: Clio — architecture: the guard is at the door
svg.desc: How Clio is guarded: the person asks, answers, approves and types secrets; the Clio service starts Pi, the agent harness, inside a bwrap jail with its own network, where only the model key exists and reaches only the provider; every effect goes through the tool host, the door, where a gateway decides each operation, a scrubber strikes secrets out, a judge (Temis, through the Jev adapter) reads outside text before the model and withholds injections, four classes of action (delete, spend, send, control) are set aside for the person, and every effect is logged with copies for undo; the vault holds secrets the model never sees; clio-memory on the left; the machine in host mode below, with copy mode as the alternative.

Sees no vault, no home folder and no Clio data. In host mode its working
folder is empty; in copy mode the copy is read-only to it.
Holds no credential but the model key, which reaches only the provider,
through the egress proxy. No jail or a failed self-test: Pi does not start.
Pi and the model are not trusted: everything below assumes they were fooled.

they stop when the session ends
Copy mode instead (--copy, "mode": "copy", clio run --workspace DIR)
The agent works on a copy of one project. bash runs in a bwrap jail with no network and no home folder, under a time limit;
credential files are not copied. You review with clio diff and bring changes back with clio apply; clio undo restores the original.
The tool host, the scrubber, the judge and the vault work the same way in both modes.
EVERYTHING IS LOGGED · FILE CHANGES CAN BE UNDONE
and after; set aside, denied and
what waits for the person; runs
what the judge kept from the
THE GUARD IS AT THE DOOR · WHAT HOLDS WHEN THE MODEL WAS FOOLED
The harness and the model stay jailed
Pi and the model never see the vault, the person's files or Clio's data. The only credential in the jail is the model key, and it reaches only the provider.
Every effect goes through the tool host
Reading, writing, running a command, the memory: each is a request to the tool host, and the gateway decides each one in code.
Outside text meets the judge first
Temis reads what a tool brought in from outside before the model does. An injection is withheld, the session becomes suspect, and its networked commands wait.
Four classes of action wait for the owner
Delete, spend, send and control are set aside, not run. The person approves each one, and it runs once, exactly as saved.
The model sees names, never values. A secret the task needs is typed by the person into the vault, and never passes through Pi, the guard or the model.
Everything is logged, and file changes can be undone
The action log has a line before and after each effect. The file tools keep a copy before they write, and clio undo walks them back.
What it does not stop: a script that gets around the list, root under the systemd launcher, daemons reached by their Unix sockets. See docs/threat-model.md.
